**My reasoning:**

I have been farming this land since I was young. My husband passed some years ago and my son works in Shijiazhuang now. I farm about 7 mu on my own, with the help of rented machines at harvest time. I have always planted winter wheat after the autumn and then summer corn on the same fields — that is what my mother did, what every family around here does. The land knows this rotation. The soil here in Quzhou is flat and we can irrigate from the wells, though my neighbor says the water table has dropped again. I do not want to try new things I do not understand at my age. If the wheat fails I have nothing.

For seed, I will buy from the agri-supply shop in town — the improved wheat seed they sell, probably Jimai 22 or whatever they recommend this year, and Zhengdan 958 corn seed, same as last year. My son sent me some money so I can afford the compound fertilizer. I will apply it the way the man at the shop told me and the same as my neighbors do — more is better for the wheat, I think, because I want a full head on every stalk.

I will water the wheat three times: once before winter sets in, once at jointing, once at heading. The corn in summer usually gets enough rain but I will irrigate once if July is dry like last year. I use the rotary tiller before I plant wheat because my neighbor rents his machine cheaply. For corn I just drop it into the stubble rows — no need to till again in summer heat.

I will spray for weeds on the wheat in winter and once more for rust or mildew in spring. Corn needs one spray for the corn borer if I see them.
